Biology 2025 Higher Level, deferred sitting: reviewed task ledger, carded for the first time.

Independent visual sweep (2026-11-19), every page rendered and read:
  * LC025ALP038EV (deferredexams/2025; Sections A and B and Answerbook), 40 pages: p1 cover, p2
    instructions, p3-p9 Section A Questions 1-7, p10-p12 Section B Questions 8-10, p13 Section C
    answerbook instructions, p14-p15 graph paper, p16-p39 ruled answer pages, p40 back cover.
  * LC025ALP040EV (Section C), 12 pages: p1 cover, p2-p10 Questions 11-17, p11 "Do not hand this
    question paper up", p12 back cover.
  * LC025ALP000EV (deferredmarkingschemes/2025), 36 pages: p1 cover, p2 the deferred-scheme note, p3
    introduction, p4-p5 marking examples, p6 the annotations table, p7-p34 Questions 1-17, p35 blank,
    p36 back cover.

The sitting has the June shape (any five of Section A, any two of B, any four of C). The deferred scheme
sets out every printed ask, so no card needs the "prints no answer" row. Q1 is best five of six at 4;
every other row carries the scheme's own mark (names 1, functions 3 and the like), the parts' totals
as printed. Choice asks the scheme answers per option are ROUTES (Q14(c)(v) asthma or bronchitis); asks
it answers on one row for either option are one card (Q5(d), Q9(b), Q17(a)(v)). Q10(b)'s one printed
ask carries eight priced rows: its method and safety rows and its labelled diagram are two cards
(items "method" and "diagram"), each under the full printed ask. The scheme's own numbering slips
(Q17(a) "(iv)" twice, Q17(c) "(iii)" twice) are mapped to the paper's parts by wording. Answers the
scheme ends with "……….", its sign for further acceptable answers, are lifted as printed. Underlined
terms (Q4(a), Q13(b)(i), Q16(a)(i)) are shown on crops of the printed passage and its ask.

q2-flower: Diagram of an animal-pollinated flower: A points to the top of the central stalk, B to the tip of one of the stalks around it, and C to one of the large outer leaves of the flower.
q3-graph: Graph of the barn owl population against time (years): the line rises and falls in a series of peaks and troughs.
q4a-question: The printed question: Sickle cell anaemia is an inherited blood condition that affects red blood cell function. It is a recessive condition caused by a mutation, with recessive and mutation underlined; then (a) Explain the underlined terms.
q5-ear: Diagram of the internal structure of the human ear: A points to the canal leading in from the outer ear, B to the thin membrane at its end, C to the small bones behind it, D to the looped canals of the inner ear, and the coiled Cochlea is labelled.
q6-bacterium: Diagram of a rod-shaped bacterium: A points to a small ring of DNA inside the cell and B to the long whip-like structures at one end.
q7-cell: Diagram of the ultrastructure of a plant cell: the Cell wall, a Nuclear pore, a Ribosome and the Vacuole are labelled, and A points to the thin layer just inside the cell wall.
q9-graphs: Two graphs of rate of photosynthesis: one against CO2 concentration and one against light intensity; each line rises and then levels off.
q11-mitosis: Diagram of a cell in metaphase of mitosis: X-shaped chromosomes lined up across the middle, with the Centromere and the Spindle labelled.
q12-figure1: Figure 1: a short section of a DNA molecule drawn as two strands joined by rungs, with the bases left blank; X and Y label two components of one strand. A key shows the shapes for cytosine and adenine.
q12-figure2: Figure 2: a section of DNA reading T A C A G G A C A.
q13b-passage: The printed passage of Question 13(b), with habitat and fauna underlined: farms wiring off corners of their fields to improve biodiversity within the habitat, new hedgerows capturing carbon dioxide, and a greater diversity of fauna; then (i) Explain the underlined terms.
q13-chain: Food chain drawn with pictures and arrows: Oak tree, Aphid, Ladybird, Dragonfly.
q14-breathing: Diagram of parts of the human breathing system without the breathing muscles: the Lung is labelled; A points to a bone around the chest, B to the windpipe, and C to one of the tubes branching from it.
q15-scientists: Photographs of the two Irish scientists who proposed a model of water transport in plants.
q15-layering: Drawing of layering: a plant stem bent down and pegged into the soil, where new roots grow from it.
q16a-passage: The printed passage of Question 16(a), with in vitro fertilisation and hormones underlined: one step of IVF is shown; other steps involve hormones to encourage super-ovulation, eggs are retrieved, and embryos are transferred to the female reproductive system; then (i) Explain the underlined terms.
q16-ivf: Image of one step of IVF: a fine needle approaching an egg (sex cell) held under a microscope.
q16d-table: Table of the botanist\u2019s data: relative IAA concentration 0, 10–1, 100, 101, 102 against root length (mm) 10, 18, 8, 3, 0 and shoot length (mm) 2, 10, 20, 30, 15.
q17-brain: Diagram of the internal structure of the human brain: A points to the large folded upper part, B to the stem at the base, C to the rounded part at the lower back, and D to the cord continuing down from the stem.
q17c-seed: Diagram of a seed with its Endosperm labelled, beside a table with columns Substrate, Enzyme and Product(s) and rows Starch, Protein and Lipid, the enzyme and product cells empty.
